title: No more bad outputs with structured generation: Remi Louf
talk_summary: Remi Louf presents Outlines, a library that constrains LLM token sampling to a target structure (regex, JSON schema, Pydantic, context-free grammar) by masking logits that would violate the structure. He argues this eliminates invalid outputs, cuts wasted tokens, and even improves accuracy of small open models on structured tasks.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of prompting/threatening the model to emit JSON, they mask logits at each step so tokens that would violate the schema/grammar cannot be sampled.
takeaways.numbers: Mistral 7B: 17.7% valid JSON without, 99.9% with structured generation

takeaways.what_they_do: Brackets and field names in JSON are known in advance, so the model need not generate them; only the variable content is sampled.
takeaways.evidence_quote: only five out of 10 tokens need to be generated so only one half
takeaways.numbers: 5 of 10 tokens generated in their example

takeaways.what_they_do: Constraining output to the answer shape removes preamble/explanation tokens the model would otherwise emit before the answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: CH GPT took 50 tokens you know it yed yed Yap and give it up 50 tokens
takeaways.numbers: 50 tokens vs 8 tokens for the same DNS answer

takeaways.technique: Structured decoding lets cheaper/smaller models match big ones
takeaways.what_they_do: Adding structure generation to a small open model raised function-calling accuracy above a larger closed model on the Berkeley function benchmark.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you add structure generation you get 96.5% and as a comparison GPT 4 ... get 93.5%

takeaways.technique: Few-shot examples teach structure, not task
takeaways.what_they_do: With structure enforced, one-shot matched eight-shot accuracy, suggesting examples mainly convey output format.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you actually get in the same ballpack in terms of accuracy with one shot as you do with eight shots

takeaways.what_they_do: Beyond syntax, constrain generation to valid identifiers (e.g., real table/column names) so generated SQL always runs.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they hallucinate table or column names ... I can guarantee you that it will run
